Dispersion (optics).fact: Dispersion is the phenomenon in which the phase velocity of a wave depends on its frequency. Sometimes the term chromatic dispersion is used to refer to optics specifically, as opposed to wave propagation in general.

Dispersion (optics).subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dispersion (optics).question: The wavelength dependence of a material's refractive index is usually quantified by its Abbe number or its coefficients in an empirical formula such as the Cauchy or _____ equations
Dispersion (optics).fact: The wavelength dependence of a material's refractive index is usually quantified by its Abbe number or its coefficients in an empirical formula such as the Cauchy or Sellmeier equations.

Dispersion (optics).subject: Meteorology & Climate

Dispersion (optics).fact: Because of the Kramers–Kronig relations, the wavelength dependence of the real part of the refractive index is related to the material absorption, described by the imaginary part of the refractive index (also called the extinction coefficient). In particular, for non-magnetic materials (μ = μ0), the susceptibility χ that appears in the Kramers–Kronig relations is the electric susceptibility χe = n2 − 1.

Dispersion (optics).subject: Meteorology & Climate

Dispersion (optics).fact: At the interface of such a material with air or vacuum (index of ~1), Snell's law predicts that light incident at an angle θ to the normal will be refracted at an angle arcsin(⁠sin θ/n⁠).

Dispersion (optics).subject: Meteorology & Climate
Dispersion (optics).question: These terms are simply a _____ series expansion of the dispersion relation β(ω) of the medium or waveguide around some particular frequency
Dispersion (optics).fact: These terms are simply a Taylor series expansion of the dispersion relation β(ω) of the medium or waveguide around some particular frequency. Their effects can be computed via numerical evaluation of Fourier transforms of the waveform, via integration of higher-order slowly varying envelope approximations, by a split-step method (which can use the exact dispersion relation rather than a Taylor series), or by direct simulation of the full Maxwell's equations rather than an approximate envelope...

Dispersion (optics).subject: Meteorology & Climate

Dispersion (optics).fact: However, as observed on Earth, the components of each pulse emitted at higher radio frequencies arrive before those emitted at lower frequencies.
